corrections.original: Report referred to the FOMC press conference and rate-path commentary as "Powell's" throughout (nine references), implying Jerome Powell remained Federal Reserve Chair.
corrections.corrected: Kevin Warsh has served as Federal Reserve Chair since May 22, 2026 (nominated by President Trump Mar 4, 2026; confirmed by the Senate 54-45 on May 12-13, 2026; sworn in May 22, 2026), succeeding Jerome Powell. Wednesday Jul 29's FOMC press conference will be led by Warsh, not Powell.
corrections.error_source: Prior edition carried forward a stale assumption about Fed leadership without verifying against a primary source; not independently checked before Sunday's publication.
corrections.note: Verified directly against federalreserve.gov press release other20260522a.htm this run. Does not change the FOMC meeting date/time, non-SEP status, or hold/hike odds framing from Sunday's edition -- only the identity of who delivers the press conference and statement. Corrected in today's report (2026-07-27-am) Top Stories and Section 20.

corrections.original: Described the US-Iran strike pause as "holding a fifth day" as of Tuesday, July 28, 2026.
corrections.corrected: Contemporaneous, dated reporting (Al Jazeera, NPR, CS Monitor, Washington Times, all dated Jul 26) describes Saturday Jul 25 as the pause's first day and Sunday Jul 26 as its "second day" on their own datelines, making Tuesday Jul 28 the pause's fourth day, not fifth.
corrections.error_source: An off-by-one day-count drift that began in the 2026-07-27-pm edition, which incremented the count on the same calendar day as that morning's edition without re-verifying the pause's actual start date against dated source reporting; today's AM edition continued the drift by one more day.
corrections.note: Verified via WebSearch against multiple outlets' own datelines this run. Does not change any prior story's substance -- only the day-count label. Corrected in today's report (2026-07-28-pm) Top Stories and Section 20.

corrections.original: This morning's edition (2026-07-31-am) did not cover President Trump's Board of Peace announcement of a Hamas disarmament agreement for Gaza, a major story that broke Thursday afternoon/evening (2026-07-30), before that edition's news cutoff.
corrections.corrected: Added to today's Closing Brief (2026-07-31-pm) Top Stories and Section 4, one news cycle late, with the coverage gap disclosed explicitly rather than the story being folded in as if newly broken.
corrections.error_source: Coverage omission, not a factual error -- this run's news-research pass for the 2026-07-31-am edition did not surface the story despite its prominence in wire coverage dated Jul 30.
corrections.note: This is a completeness gap, not an inaccurate statement previously published. Logged per SR SS9 for transparency; no prior published sentence needed correcting, so no diff against prior report text is shown.

corrections.original: Named the Saudi-led Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance's 14 founding countries as Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Yemen, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Sudan, Djibouti, and Somalia.
corrections.corrected: Multiple wire sources describing the actual July 30 charter-signing joint declaration (Saudi Gazette, Anadolu Agency, Arabian Business, Middle East Monitor) instead list Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, Egypt, Pakistan, Turkiye, Djibouti, Somalia, Bangladesh, Yemen, and the Comoros as the 14 founding/signatory states -- Nigeria and Sudan do not appear among the charter signatories; the Comoros does.
corrections.error_source: The Thursday edition's list appears to have reflected an earlier or broader roster (possibly drawn from the wider 43-nation planning talks) rather than the smaller charter-signing roster confirmed once the alliance's founding declaration was actually issued Jul 30.
corrections.note: Verified via WebSearch against multiple wire sources this run (2026-08-01-sat). Does not change the story's substance -- the alliance's formation, headquarters, and purpose are unaffected -- only the named country roster. Corrected in today's report (2026-08-01-sat) Top Story 9 and Section 29.
